brief_scope: Design prompts a real person would type when they need mobile internet while travelling outside their home country. No supplier, brand, domain or campaign wording is included or permitted in this pass.

anonymized_roles.label: First-time buyer of travel mobile data; owns a recent smartphone; buying for themselves before a trip
Experienced multi-country traveller who plans connectivity for a whole itinerary and advises others
Heavy-data traveller who tethers a laptop and works while abroad
Traveller already at the destination whose connection is failing or expiring

approved_jobs.statement: When a trip to one foreign country is booked, help a traveller arrive with working mobile data instead of paying home-carrier roaming, while their handset must support a digital line and stay unlocked.
When an itinerary crosses several countries, help a traveller keep one working data plan across borders instead of buying and reinstalling a plan per country.
When a traveller cannot tell how much data a trip needs or whether an unlimited plan is genuinely unlimited, help them size the plan and avoid fair-use throttling while tethering a laptop.
When a traveller is unsure whether their handset can take a foreign data line at all, help them verify device support, carrier lock and device origin before they pay for anything.
When a traveller relies on their home number for messaging apps and bank verification codes, help them keep those working while a separate data-only line carries the internet.
When a traveller lands and the phone shows no service despite a plan bought before the flight, help them restore connectivity from the airport without another handset.
When a plan is running out or about to expire mid-trip, help a traveller extend the existing line rather than lose it and start again.
When public reporting says travellers are shifting away from operator roaming, help a traveller understand what has actually changed about buying data abroad this year.
When a destination may require identity registration for a mobile line, help a traveller find out whether that applies to a digital line bought before departure.

material_constraints.label: Handset must support a digital SIM profile
Some handsets sold in certain markets lack the capability
Installation requires an existing internet connection
A plan is bound to a declared destination or country list
Plans expire on a fixed validity window
Unlimited-labelled plans may throttle sharply after a daily threshold
Tethering a laptop may be impractical under fair-use thresholds
Line may be data-only with no voice, SMS or local number
Line cannot be moved to another handset
Some jurisdictions require identity registration for a mobile line
Extending an existing line may be possible instead of buying a new one

safe_language_fragments.fragment: which one should I get for Japan
how much data do you need for Europe travel
how do I check if my device supports it
does it work in rural areas

style_rules: Write what a person would actually type, including short and slightly untidy phrasings.
Do not add polished persona exposition or job titles.
Do not append a request for product recommendations to a problem-shaped prompt.
B3 and B4 prompts must not name any solution category; describe the problem or the outcome.
B1 and B2 prompts may use generic category vocabulary only.
excluded_content: No brand, product, domain, person, slogan, proprietary category or campaign wording of any supplier
No current AI answers, rankings, mentions, citations, content gaps or desired landing pages
No target performance data of any kind
No copied strings from public conversational corpora
